body:
**Tier 2 — test cleanup.**

## Problem
`crates/mori-core/src/sherlock/normal_oracles.rs` (about 1.5k lines) and `extra_normal_oracles.rs` (about 2k lines) are unformatted Rust literals. `models/sherlock/reference/check-reference.py` (`serialize_oracles`) generates them from `models/sherlock/oracles/*.json`, and the tests pull them in with `include!`. The check that keeps them equal to the JSON runs only in Python, never in `cargo test`.

## Suggested fix
Copy the oracle JSON into `crates/fixtures/sherlock/` (or the `mori-sherlock` crate after #79), deserialize it with serde into the snapshot types, and delete the generated `.rs` files. Keep the oracles as data: they are independent expectations, so insta snapshots would be the wrong tool. Add a test that the fixture copies match `models/sherlock/oracles/*.json` byte for byte, or generate one from the other.

## Needs input
Which copy is the source of truth: `models/sherlock/oracles/` or the crate fixtures.

## Done when
No generated Rust oracle files remain, and `cargo test` alone catches drift between the oracles and the JSON.

---
**Working on this:** builds on #74. Read `RUST_GUIDELINES.md` and `plugins/moriarty-dev/skills/develop/references/rust.md` first; a deviation from the guidelines needs agreement before it's made. Before handing off, all of these pass:

```
cargo fmt --all --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace
```
title: Rust: load Sherlock oracles from JSON instead of generated Rust
